title: Mark Up a PDF Without Printing It: Comments, Highlights and Arrows
description: You don't need Acrobat to leave feedback on a PDF. Here's how to highlight, comment and mark up documents free in the browser.
excerpt: "Can you mark up this PDF?" doesn't have to mean printing, scribbling and scanning. Do it on screen in two minutes, for free.
content:
Someone shares a document and asks for your feedback. The old reflex is to print it, scribble in the margins, and scan it back. There is a far faster way that keeps your notes legible and your feedback easy to act on.

**Annotating means marking up, not editing**

You do not need to change the document's text to give feedback — you need to point at things. Highlights flag the important lines. Comment notes explain what should change. Arrows and boxes draw attention to a specific spot. All of it sits on top of the PDF without altering the original.

**The free workflow**

1. **Open the PDF in the browser.** Upload it to [FileTools](https://filetools.eu) — no account, no software install.
2. **Highlight and comment.** Mark the passages that matter and drop notes explaining your feedback.
3. **Export and send back** a single annotated PDF the other person can open anywhere.

**Why this beats print-and-scan**

Handwritten margin notes are often unreadable and always slower. Typed comments are clear, searchable, and land as a clean document rather than a crooked phone photo of a printout. And because [FileTools](https://filetools.eu) works in the browser, a confidential contract or draft is not uploaded to someone's servers.

**If the PDF is locked**

Some PDFs are restricted so you cannot mark them up. Unlock it first with [FileTools](https://filetools.eu/pdf-unlock), then annotate as normal.

Reviewing a document should take minutes, not a trip to the printer. Highlight, comment, send — and your feedback arrives clear and easy to act on.
